logs.speaker: TECH L. MARQUEZ
logs.text: Transfer request, filed again. That's three. Eleven years in the farms, and I've never seen a crop lean. Since we parked over Ruin, everything in the Orchard Dome leans down. Not toward the lamps. Toward the deck plating. Toward the moon. Put me on the docking ring. I don't care what the job is.

logs.speaker: DR. N. OKAFOR
logs.text: Sample protocol, Hydroponics. Collect in pairs. Gloves, mask, sealed jars, and burn anything that touches bare skin. Tissue from the farm cases keeps growing in the jar. It doesn't need light. It doesn't need water. It grows toward whoever is holding it.

logs.header: AUDIO LOG // CORWIN SABLE, GORGON LIAISON
logs.speaker: CORWIN SABLE, GORGON LIAISON
logs.text: Memo to Gorgon Consolidated, Asset Division. Hydroponics yield is up two hundred percent since arrival at Ruin. The new growth is not edible, and it is not to be destroyed. Agricultural staff will remain on shift inside the sealed farms to maintain it. Classify the farms as a yield retention site. Transfers out of agriculture are suspended from today.

logs.speaker: TECH L. MARQUEZ
logs.text: Inventory. The heirloom wheat sprouted inside sealed canisters. No water, no light, minus twenty in the cold store. I opened one to check, and every shoot turned toward my hand at once. I've moved the clean stock to the vault behind the racks and taped the seams. If anyone asks, the cold store failed.

logs.header: AUDIO LOG // SR. AGRONOMIST H. LINDQVIST
logs.speaker: SR. AGRONOMIST H. LINDQVIST
logs.text: Harvest log, orchard rows one to six. We picked the trees bare on Tuesday. By Thursday the fruit was back, full size, and warm. Nobody's eating it. Doctor Okafor took samples and asked us to stop pruning, because every cut grows back as two. The trees don't drop their leaves anymore. They hold on to everything.

logs.speaker: TECH L. MARQUEZ
logs.text: The old fig in the middle of the dome. Forty years old, older than the ship. Last night its roots went through the planter and into the deck. I put my ear to the plating, and I could hear it. Like a crowd humming in another room. It stopped when I said its name.

logs.header: AUDIO LOG // SR. AGRONOMIST H. LINDQVIST
logs.speaker: SR. AGRONOMIST H. LINDQVIST
logs.text: We tried to clear the bottom terrace with shears. Kessler cut through a root as thick as my arm, and it closed up behind the blades. Then it found his boot. It took four of us to pull him loose, and his leg came out green under the skin. Okafor says only fire stops it. Facilities is sending the purge torch up from stores.

logs.speaker: AGRONOMIST D. CASTELLANOS
logs.text: I'm in the mushroom beds at the back of the caves. It's dark and wet, and they don't come in here much. The ones that used to be my crew stand very still in the rows, with roots coming out of their sleeves. When the lamps flicker, they lean toward the light. When it's dark, they lean toward me.

logs.speaker: AGRONOMIST D. CASTELLANOS
logs.text: My lamp is dying. The rooted ones have moved two rows closer since I last checked. If you find this, the scrubber valve for this wing is on the west wall, and someone shut it by hand. That wasn't a fault. Ro, if this gets to you, I tried to come home.

logs.speaker: TECH L. MARQUEZ
logs.text: I found Abernathy from night shift. He's standing in the oyster beds where he fell asleep. The roots came up through the bed and into him while he slept. His eyes followed me down the row. I cut one root to free him, and it grew back before I'd stepped away. I left him there. I'm sorry, Paul.

logs.header: AUDIO LOG // LIFE-SUPPORT TECH R. HADDAD
logs.speaker: LIFE-SUPPORT TECH R. HADDAD
logs.text: Scrubber Hall, status. All three scrubbers report fault codes, but the faults aren't real. Somebody shut the valves by hand, one in each wing, and taped over the indicators. Carbon dioxide in the farms is climbing, and the growth likes it. I'm going to open them back up, one wing at a time, if the things in the rows let me.

logs.header: AUDIO LOG // LIFE-SUPPORT TECH R. HADDAD
logs.speaker: LIFE-SUPPORT TECH R. HADDAD
logs.text: Atmosphere Control. The order to shut the scrubbers came from the liaison's office, signed by Sable. Reason given: yield retention. I called up to ask what that means. He said the farms are company property, and so is the air in them. The console won't vent while the scrubbers are down. All three valves first. Then vent.

logs.speaker: TECH L. MARQUEZ
logs.text: Last entry from the farms. The irrigation lines are singing. Low, under the pumps, all day long. Ruiz says it's air in the pipes. Ruiz has also stopped sleeping. My transfer to the docking ring came through, and I'm taking it tonight. Whatever is growing down here, I won't be its gardener.
